tasks.short: Write website specifications that explain required behaviour, content, interfaces and technical constraints.

steps.what: Gather the campaign brief, page requirements and existing specifications.
Inspect technical settings in the {CMS} and code repository in {OTHER}.
Agree user journeys, scope and acceptance criteria with the marketing manager and developer.
Write the website specification using the agreed scope and technical inventory.

loop.input: Approved scope, acceptance criteria, technical inventory and specification template.
loop.output: Website specification draft with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required sections and technical facts; designer checks meaning and unsupported commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per specification; unresolved sections return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates populate technical facts, but agreed behaviour needs prose drawn from varied briefs.

steps.what: Review feasibility, interfaces and acceptance criteria before accepting the specification.
Send the approved specification link to the delivery team.

tasks.design: Link approved inputs from {PROJECT} and {DOCS}, then generate a technical inventory from {CMS} and the code repository in {OTHER}. A bounded drafting loop fills a specification template in {DOCS}; designer and developer approvals release the version and trigger a {PROJECT} notification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were scattered, technical facts changed, and prose needed interpretation. Maintaining a custom generator often cost more than writing occasional specifications.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates, repository metadata and small integrations can supply reliable facts. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, while a bounded model handles variable prose.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting requirements, hidden dependencies and realistic acceptance criteria still need discussion. Faster drafting does not establish feasibility.
tasks.human_edge: The designer connects user needs, brand intent and technical limits, and exposes trade-offs stakeholders have missed.

ambition.what: Pre-build accessibility and feasibility brief for campaign landing pages

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling specifications toward resolving scope and accessibility questions earlier. No approval rights change automatically.

reach.task: Turn a campaign objective into a testable landing-page brief.
reach.learn: Campaign economics, audience priorities and which conversion measures support a scope decision.
Documentation structure, terminology control and source traceability.

evidence.claim: Template generation and structured technical extraction are feasible; the proposed specification workflow is an extrapolation.
GitHub Copilot supports code completion and review with human oversight; this supports building the generator.
Developer field trials reported productivity gains, but they do not establish a 10–100-fold gain for specification work.

assumptions: Time shares describe a typical mixed technical and marketing specification, not a measured customer baseline.
A shared specification template and readable technical settings exist.
The pilot covers one website and one specification format.
The priors favour generation, but scope agreement and technical acceptance retain substantial human work.
Access estimates include permission review. Consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time if staff monitoring is introduced.
GDPR applies to personal information in briefs; EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual deployment.
unknowns: Where specifications and code are stored.
Which technical settings can be accessed without exposing secrets.
Who approves scope and technical feasibility.
Whether briefs contain personal or confidential information.
research_questions: Which specification fields can be generated directly from maintained technical sources?
Does drafting reduce total effort after review and correction?
Which recurring ambiguities should become structured brief fields?
new_work: Review generated prose and unresolved questions.
Maintain templates and technical extraction mappings.
Handle unavailable sources and conflicting versions.
Check that approved specifications remain linked to their source versions.

tasks.short: Record website performance, capacity and browser or device usage for design and development decisions.

steps.what: Read hosting, database and web analytics dashboards in {OTHER}.
Align reporting periods, units and browser categories in a workbook.
Discuss unusual readings and technical constraints with the operations team.
Write the technical report with charts, reporting dates and agreed explanations.
Share the technical report with the developer and marketing manager.

tasks.design: Use configured exports from monitoring and analytics in {OTHER}, with a scheduled job on {DATA_PLATFORM} to align units, periods and categories. Feed a {BI} dashboard and generate dated reports in {DOCS}, inserting human explanations verbatim and notifying the team through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metrics came from separate systems with different units and reporting windows. Occasional reports did not justify maintaining the connections.
tasks.enabler_now: Available exports, scheduled jobs and reusable report templates make the work mostly deterministic. No model loop is needed for factual documentation.
tasks.still_hard: Missing telemetry, misleading aggregates and separating design problems from infrastructure problems remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The designer judges whether a technical limit harms a real user journey and asks the operations team the right questions.

ambition.what: Weekly mobile performance triage for campaign landing pages

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time copying metrics and more time investigating user-facing bottlenecks. Infrastructure changes and campaign priorities keep their existing approval owners.

reach.learn: Search performance measures, measurement uncertainty and the difference between correlation and causation.

reach.task: Interpret device usage across audience segments.
reach.learn: Sampling bias, small-group suppression and defensible comparisons.

evidence.claim: Scheduled collection, metric normalization and template reports can automate structured documentation without a model.
GDPR requires appropriate handling of personal data in analytics; national consultation rules may apply to staff monitoring.

assumptions: The designer documents existing measurements; collecting new telemetry is outside the pilot.
A workbook currently bridges monitoring and analytics sources.
The estimates cover a small set of metrics for one website.
The human-task prior is outweighed by structured collection and reporting steps; interpretation remains human.
Reports use aggregate device categories and omit visitor identifiers.
Access estimates include privacy review and initial consultation where applicable; national procedures can extend elapsed time.
EU AI Act obligations must be assessed if a model is later added.
unknowns: Whether hosting and database metrics are available to the designer.
Which sources offer scheduled exports or supported interfaces.
Whether analytics currently identifies visitors or employees.
Which reporting periods and thresholds the team trusts.
Whether national employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which metrics influence an actual design decision?
Can missing or stale data be detected before a report is issued?
Would an existing dashboard remove the need for a separate report?
new_work: Investigate stale data and failed collection.
Maintain metric definitions and category mappings.
Review unusual trends with the operations team.
Maintain access, retention and aggregation settings.

tasks.short: Define and implement a repeatable process for reviewing, approving and publishing website revisions.

steps.what: Review revision requests, previous problems and the current publishing procedure.
Draft revision categories, review stages, checks and rollback instructions.

loop.input: Selected revision issues, current procedure, approved requirements and procedure template.
loop.output: Procedure draft with proposed stages and explicitly unresolved policy choices.
loop.check: Check required sections and source references; designer verifies controls and executable rollback instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved ownership or risk choices go to the meeting.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template provides structure, but varied incident narratives need synthesis into proposed instructions.

steps.what: Agree approval roles, revision risk categories and escalation with the marketing manager and developer.
Configure revision forms, approval stages and publishing permissions in the {CMS}.
Test approvals, previews and rollback using browser testing tools in {OTHER}.
Publish the approved procedure internally and notify content contributors.

tasks.design: Configure revision forms and approval stages in {CMS} and {WORKFLOW}, linked to a versioned procedure in {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts procedure changes from selected issues, while deterministic tests exercise permissions, previews and rollback; public revisions retain the approval actions defined for their risk category.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures lived apart from publishing controls, and exception handling depended on experienced people. Maintaining tests and approval mappings took sustained effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing publishing controls can often be configured, with small coded checks filling gaps. Bounded drafting reduces document preparation without deciding publication policy.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent changes, conflicting owners, accessibility judgement and genuine rollback across connected systems remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: The designer balances speed, brand quality, accessibility and the consequences of a mistaken publication.

ambition.what: Guided event-page revision service for event planners

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward difficult revisions and improving contributor guidance. Event planners can gain draft and preview access after explicit delegation; final publication rights follow approved risk categories.

reach.task: Approve content revisions through a staged publishing process.
reach.learn: Editorial acceptance criteria, correction handling and version discipline.
Event information dependencies, deadlines and common last-minute changes.

evidence.claim: Configured publishing stages, permissions and deterministic checks can implement much of a revision procedure.
Playwright Test Agents can generate test plans and tests; the proposed routine checks can run deterministically.
Reported security failures in generated code support testing custom workflow code before use.

assumptions: The pilot covers one website, a small set of revision categories and existing staging facilities.
The current {CMS} supports roles, previews and version history.
Public publishing remains a separately authorized action.
The workflow prior fits execution, but deciding approval policy remains human.
Access estimates include role approval and contributor onboarding.
GDPR applies to request records; consultation under national rules may be needed if audit logs become staff monitoring.
EU AI Act obligations depend on how the drafting component is deployed.
unknowns: Which approval and rollback capabilities the current {CMS} supports.
Which revisions require legal, editorial or accessibility approval.
Whether contributors need new access or employee consultation.
Whether connected forms and campaigns can be rolled back with pages.
research_questions: Which revision categories can use existing controls without custom code?
Can a dry run demonstrate that unauthorized publication is blocked?
Which exceptions cause contributors to bypass the procedure?
new_work: Review procedure drafts and unresolved policy choices.
Maintain approval mappings and contributor permissions.
Handle urgent revisions and failed checks.
Retest the workflow after configuration changes.
Update guidance when recurring exceptions reveal a missing revision category.

tasks.short: Verify website ownership, provide a sitemap and check search-engine discovery and indexing.

steps.what: Check existing property verification and discovery settings in search consoles in {OTHER}.
Verify site ownership through the {CMS} or domain administration tools in {OTHER}.
Generate and validate a sitemap for the website's intended public pages.
Submit the sitemap address through search consoles in {OTHER}.
Review crawl diagnostics and distinguish intended exclusions from indexing problems.

tasks.design: Configure sitemap generation and validation in {CMS}, and retain ownership records and approved indexing rules in {DOCS}. Use existing search-console reports in {OTHER} to surface exceptions; people confirm ownership changes and initial submissions, while stable sitemap discovery removes unnecessary repeat registration.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verification needed privileged access, and search consoles offered uneven automation. The task happens too rarely to justify elaborate integration.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing sitemap generation and console reporting already cover much of the work. Reusable instructions and validation remove preparation without needing a model or agent.
tasks.still_hard: Ownership disputes, unsupported console interfaces and interpreting delayed indexing remain human work. Submission does not guarantee indexing, ranking or traffic.
tasks.human_edge: The designer knows which pages should be discoverable and coordinates technical fixes with search strategy.
tasks.altitude: Occasional registration takes less preparation, with more attention on indexing exceptions. No decision rights change, and the overall week changes little.

reach.task: Prioritise fixes for important pages excluded from search results.
reach.learn: Canonical URLs, crawl controls, intended exclusions and the limits of indexing reports.

reach.task: Check discovery of product and category pages.
reach.learn: Catalogue update patterns, duplicate pages and commercial page priorities.

evidence.claim: Ownership verification, sitemap generation and search-console diagnostics are established website administration practices.
Search submission supports discovery but does not guarantee indexing or improved ranking.

assumptions: This describes modern search-property verification and sitemap submission rather than legacy directory registration.
The {CMS} already provides sitemap generation and the search consoles provide usable reports.
The screen-based workflow is more plausible than the document-heavy means prior for this task.
Existing tools cover the pilot without additional paid infrastructure.
The administrator has approved authority over the domain.
Access estimates cover property permissions; employee consultation is not expected unless staff monitoring is added.
GDPR applies to account records. The proposed workflow contains no AI component requiring a new EU AI Act assessment.
unknowns: Which search properties are already verified.
Who controls domain administration and console access.
Whether sitemap generation is already enabled.
Whether reports can be shared using existing permissions.
research_questions: Is any registration work still necessary for established properties?
Can existing sitemap discovery eliminate repeat submissions?
Which diagnostic exceptions need a designer rather than a developer or search specialist?
new_work: Review indexing exceptions after major website changes.
Update sitemap exclusions when page types change.
Handle failed verification and delayed crawl reports.

role.altitude: The designer spends less time assembling documents and copying technical facts, and more time resolving user journeys, accessibility issues and publication trade-offs. Existing scope and publication approvals remain; any wider authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Help marketing managers prepare measurable landing-page briefs.
Work with search marketing strategists on performance and indexing priorities.
Help editors and event planners use guided revision and preview workflows.
skills_to_grow: Structured requirements and testable acceptance criteria
Accessible interaction design and manual accessibility evaluation
Review of generated prose and technical evidence
role.ambitious_version: Provide a repeatable campaign-page readiness service: an early feasibility and accessibility brief, guided contributor revisions, and weekly performance triage tied to campaign decisions.
